chunks: As for what al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Mansur, who said:

I said to Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: A slaughtered bird was given to us as a gift in Makkah, and our family ate it. He said: The people of Makkah do not consider there to be any harm in it. I said: Then what do you say? He said: Its price is upon them.

So it is understood to mean that it had been slaughtered within the Haram. There is nothing in the report stating whether it was slaughtered in the hill or in the Haram. When that is not apparent from its wording, and there are reports that contain a detailed clarification of its meaning, then acting upon them is more appropriate. We have already presented some of them, and what follows increases that clarification.

key_terms.الْأَخْبَارِ: reports; narrations used to clarify the ruling
key_terms.الْحَرَمِ: the sacred sanctuary; the inviolable precinct with special legal rulings
key_terms.الْحِلِّ: the area outside the sacred sanctuary
key_terms.بَأْسًا: harm or objection; meaning legal blame or prohibition
key_terms.ثَمَنُهُ: its price; the compensation due for it
key_terms.مَذْبُوحٌ: slaughtered; referring to the bird that had already been killed
key_terms.مَكَّةَ: Makkah; the sacred city in which the event took place

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on eating game slaughtered in Makkah or the Haram according to Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This report addresses the ruling concerning a hunted bird slaughtered in Makkah and eaten by a family, with Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام ruling that compensation in its value is due. The compiler then explains that the report is to be understood in light of other narrations, especially regarding whether the animal was slaughtered within the Haram, showing a juristic method of reconciling reports.
